definitions.explanation: To fail to win in a game, competition, or conflict.
To concede or surrender to pressure or temptation.
Colloquially, to reduce the price as a favor.

examples.japanese: {誘惑|ゆうわく}に{負|ま}けてしまった。
{少|すこ}し{負|ま}けてくれませんか。
examples.english: Could you give me a small discount?

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}いだから、いつも{最後|さいご}まで{頑張|がんば}る。
examples.english: He hates losing, so he always gives it his all until the end.
examples.notes: 負けず嫌い = competitive, hates to lose

examples.japanese: {暑|あつ}さに{負|ま}けないで、{水分|すいぶん}をしっかり{取|と}って、{夏|なつ}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えよう。
examples.english: Don't give in to the heat—stay hydrated and get through the summer.

examples.japanese: じゃんけんで{負|ま}けた。
{負|ま}けても{諦|あきら}めない。
examples.english: Even if I lose, I won't give up.
I gave in to the cold.

examples.japanese: {圧力|あつりょく}に{負|ま}けた。
{病気|びょうき}に{負|ま}けないで。
examples.english: Don't give in to the illness.

examples.japanese: {値段|ねだん}を{負|ま}けてください。
もう{少|すこ}し{負|ま}けてよ。
examples.english: Give me a bit more discount.

examples.japanese: {千円|せんえん}{負|ま}けてあげる。
examples.english: I'll give you a 1000 yen discount.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pattern: Xに{負|ま}ける (lose to X).

ASPECT: ている indicates resulting state. {負|ま}けている = 'is losing' or 'has lost.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{試合|しあい}に{負|ま}ける (lose a game)
・{相手|あいて}に{負|ま}ける (lose to an opponent)
・{誘惑|ゆうわく}に{負|ま}ける (yield to temptation)
・{負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}い (competitive, hates to lose)
・{負|ま}け{犬|いぬ} (loser—lit. 'losing dog')

OPPOSITE: {勝|か}つ (to win)

DISCOUNT USAGE (colloquial):
・{負|ま}けてよ (Give me a discount!)
・{負|ま}けてあげる (I'll give you a discount)
